reviews.lens: STATE-L1 end to end — the full slider-gesture lifecycle (press/hold/release, cover swipe mid-hold, HUD teardown mid-drag, rapid re-grab after cancel, multi-slider hand-off) walked against the round-3 code, plus a regression sweep of the whole ~200-line diff (git show HEAD = cf3d43d).

closureVerdicts.item: 1. STATE-L1 — gestureHeld liveness, held-gesture expiry immunity, 30 s backstop, re-bind refusal
closureVerdicts.trace: CLOSED half: beginLiveEdit (GeoARSessionManager.swift:451-455) is wired to all three sliders' onEditingChanged(true) (ARScreen.swift:504, 531, 558); gestureAbandoned (:472-477) is pure and held-aware; the expiry call site (:1150-1155) now passes held, so a stationary 10 s hold no longer expires — the round-2 defect (expiry clears editingDropID under a live finger, next tick re-binds to a different drop) is genuinely dead. commit clears the flag (:1968), cancelLiveEdit clears it first thing (:461) so the early-return guard at :462 can't skip it, and markCameraHidden→cancelLiveEdit (:578) covers the cover-swipe case. NOT closed: the re-bind refusal at :1962-1965 is a boolean gate on a shared, latchable flag — it refuses the one legitimate non-gesture caller (F-D3-01), it can latch true with no finger down because the only clear-by-timer is gated on editingDropID != nil (F-D3-03), and one boolean cannot represent two concurrent slider gestures (F-D3-04). Lens sub-case 'rapid re-grab after cancel': legitimate NEW gestures do start cleanly — beginLiveEdit captures nearestDrop, and updateNearest (:1608-1612) unfreezes the moment cancelLiveEdit nils editingDropID; the capture can be up to one 400 ms tick stale, but the HUD (ARScreen.swift:289, 601, 605) reads the same stale nearestDrop, so the user edits the drop the panel is showing. Not a finding.

findings.title: The re-bind refusal kills "Place on ground": snapNearestDropToGround's commit is refused because no gesture is held
findings.trace: ARScreen.swift:570-572 Button → snapNearestDropToGround (GeoARSessionManager.swift:2073). The truth chain resolves groundY (:2085-2105), then :2124 calls adjustNearestDrop(height:commit: true). At that instant editingDropID == nil (it is set ONLY in beginLiveEdit:454 and adjustNearestDrop:1964, and is nilled after every commit at :2041, by cancelLiveEdit:464, and by removePerDropState:1591) and gestureHeld == false (set true ONLY by beginLiveEdit:452, which only the three sliders' onEditingChanged(true) call — ARScreen.swift:504/531/558 — and cleared on every commit at :1968). So :1962 enters and :1963 `guard gestureHeld else { return }` returns before ANY mutation. Verified there is no other setter of gestureHeld and no other caller of adjustNearestDrop besides the three sliders and this snap (repo-wide grep). relocateNearestDrop (:2158) does not route through adjustNearestDrop and is unaffected.
findings.harm: The flagship ADR-027 placement fix is a no-op on tap: holder.position.y is never adjusted (:1991-1993 unreached), placedDrops[id].heightAboveGround is never updated (:1981-1984), and library.update(persist: true) is never issued (:2030-2036) — so the snap is lost on restart and never reaches other viewers or Firestore. Worse, the caller proceeds to set groundLockBaseY[drop.id] at :2126 anyway, so the session-local lock is applied later by the GPS refresh (:1802) or the next VPS transform (:931) — the object silently drifts to the measured ground minutes later while the persisted height and the height slider (ARScreen.swift:572 syncSliders → :605-608 reads the unchanged model) still read the old value. Tap-does-nothing, then moves-by-itself, then reverts on relaunch. This is a regression introduced by this diff: before round 3 the unconditional capture at the old :1959 made the snap bind and commit normally.
findings.fix: Do not route a non-gesture edit through the gesture-capture gate. Split the body: `private func applyEdit(to id: UUID, height: Double?, scale: Double?, rotation: Double?, commit: Bool)` holding everything from the current :1966 onward; `adjustNearestDrop` resolves the id under the gesture rules (capture from beginLiveEdit, refusal when unheld) and delegates; `snapNearestDropToGround` calls `applyEdit(to: drop.id, height: …, commit: true)` with the id it already holds at :2074. Expose the binding decision as a pure `nonisolated static func editBinding(capture: UUID?, held: Bool, explicitTarget: UUID?, nearest: UUID?) -> UUID?` so it is table-testable off the MainActor class.

findings.title: The new resume-plan `cameraVisible` conjunct is invariantly false — every warm resume drops the mesh and immediately re-runs the session
findings.trace: resumeSession (:509) is called from exactly one place: ARSessionHolder.startIfNeeded:104, under `else if !sessionRunning`. sessionRunning becomes false only in suspend():121-125, which calls manager.suspendSession():423 → `cameraVisible = false` (:426). The three paths into startIfNeeded all leave the manager's flag false at plan time: beginRevealWarmup:55-59 (camera genuinely hidden), cameraDidAppear:61-66 (startIfNeeded at :64 runs BEFORE markCameraVisible at :65), appDidBecomeActive:87-91 (startIfNeeded at :89 before markCameraVisible at :90). Hence :543-550 always yields reconstruction == false; :551 records it in appliedPerception and :552 runs a config without sceneReconstruction. startTicking() (:563) then schedules tick() (:1042-1050), which on the next runloop turn — after markCameraVisible has already executed synchronously — computes perceptionPlan reconstruction = true (:1338-1341, cameraRecentlyVisible true) and setPerception (:852-865) sees desired != applied and fires a SECOND arView.session.run at :856.
findings.harm: Two ARKit reconfigurations back-to-back at the reveal instant, which is exactly the TTFO/killer-#1 measurement point, and sessionRunSince is reset twice (:561 and :864), re-arming the ADR-043 reveal gate. Because run #1 disables sceneReconstruction, ARKit drops the mesh anchors the retained world map was holding, so every tab-flip resume rebuilds the LiDAR mesh from zero — the multi-second occlusion hole (content drawing over real geometry, the wave's draw-over bar) that ARPCFG-4 and this same commit's hide-edge stamp exist to prevent. Before this diff the resume plan requested reconstruction and the mesh survived the resume.
findings.fix: Pass the intent instead of reading a flag that is false by construction: `func resumeSession(cameraIntended: Bool)` and call `manager.resumeSession(cameraIntended: cameraVisible)` from ARSessionHolder.startIfNeeded (the holder's own flag is already true at ARSessionHolder.swift:62 before startIfNeeded at :64, and guarded true at :88). Equivalent minimal alternative: move `manager.markCameraVisible()` above `startIfNeeded()` in both cameraDidAppear and appDidBecomeActive. Then extract `nonisolated static func resumeReconstruction(supportsMesh:cameraIntended:pedestrian:thermalCritical:) -> Bool` so the term is table-tested rather than asserted.

findings.title: gestureHeld can latch true with no finger down — the only timer that clears it is gated on editingDropID != nil
findings.trace: The expiry at :1150-1155 is `if editingDropID != nil, gestureAbandoned(...)` — when editingDropID is nil the flag is never re-examined. Two reachable ways to reach (held == true, capture == nil): (a) beginLiveEdit:451-455 sets gestureHeld = true unconditionally but captures nothing when nearestDrop is nil; the release commit then hits `guard let id = editingDropID else { return }` at :1966, which returns BEFORE `if commit { gestureHeld = false }` at :1968. (b) A drop removed mid-drag: removePerDropState:1579-1601 clears editingDropID (:1591) and liveEditingDrops (:1590) and nils nearestDrop (:1598-1600), so the panel's gate (ARScreen.swift:289 `manager.nearestDrop != nil`) tears the Slider down mid-touch — the exact case round 2 built the abandonment timer for — and no onEditingChanged(false) arrives, leaving gestureHeld true forever. The latch survives until the next markCameraHidden:578 or suspendSession:441.
findings.harm: While latched, three things go wrong at once. (i) The re-bind refusal at :1963 is disabled, so any stale tick captures whatever nearestDrop happens to be and drives it through the persist path at :2030-2036 — a wrong-drop write to disk and Firestore, the precise harm STATE-L1 was created to eliminate. (ii) The next gesture that loses its end event gets the 30 s backstop instead of the 1.5 s expiry, holding liveEditingDrops non-empty → PowerGovernor.swift:62-65 isLiveEditing → tier .full for 30 s with nearest frozen (:1612) — a thermal/fps cost against the wave's own bars. (iii) snapNearestDropToGround (F-D3-01) succeeds only while the flag is latched, so the same tap has two different outcomes depending on invisible history.
findings.fix: Make the clear unconditional and the timer ungated: clear the held flag inside removePerDropState when `editingDropID == id`; move the commit clear above the `guard let id` return at :1966; and change the expiry condition at :1150 to `if editingDropID != nil || gestureHeld` so abandonment is evaluated whenever any gesture state is outstanding. Combine with F-D3-04's counter.

findings.title: Multi-slider hand-off: committing one slider kills a still-live drag on another
findings.trace: gestureHeld is a single Bool shared by three independently draggable Sliders (ARScreen.swift:489-562 — separate views, so iOS delivers concurrent touches to both). Sequence: finger A presses height → beginLiveEdit:452 sets gestureHeld = true, :454 captures X; finger B presses scale → beginLiveEdit:452 (flag already true, :454 skipped since editingDropID != nil — correct, same drop); finger A releases → adjustNearestDrop(height:commit: true) → :1968 sets gestureHeld = false and :2041 sets editingDropID = nil. Finger B is still down: its next tick (ARScreen.swift:521, commit: false) hits :1962 with capture nil and :1963 with held false → return. Every remaining scale tick is refused, and finger B's own release commit is refused identically.
findings.harm: A live edit dies mid-gesture and is silently discarded. The thumb keeps moving because ARScreen's liveScale is @State (ARScreen.swift:519-520), so the HUD reads ×N while the AR content never changes and nothing is persisted; the value snaps back at the next syncSliders (ARScreen.swift:601/604-608). To the user the size slider simply stops working until they lift and re-grab. The same shape occurs if the 'Place on ground' button is tapped with a slider held (the snap's commit at :2124 clears the flag out from under the live drag).
findings.fix: Model liveness as gesture depth, not a boolean: `private var heldGestures = 0`; beginLiveEdit does `heldGestures += 1`; commit and cancelLiveEdit do `heldGestures = max(0, heldGestures - 1)` and `heldGestures = 0` respectively; `gestureHeld` becomes the computed `heldGestures > 0`. Keep editingDropID as the single shared capture — two fingers on the same panel are editing the same drop, which is the correct semantics. Feed the counter through the same pure `gestureAbandoned(now:lastTick:held:)` so the caller-clock rule still holds.

testCases.name: testGroundSnapBindsWithoutAHeldGesture
testCases.asserts: On the extracted pure binder: editBinding(capture: nil, held: false, explicitTarget: X, nearest: Y) == X (an explicit caller-supplied target always binds); editBinding(capture: nil, held: false, explicitTarget: nil, nearest: Y) == nil (the re-bind refusal survives — vacuity guard: a binder that simply returns `nearest` fails this row); editBinding(capture: X, held: true, explicitTarget: nil, nearest: Y) == X (a live capture is never overridden by a moved nearest — vacuity guard: a binder that returns `explicitTarget ?? nearest` fails this row).
testCases.failsWhen: Fails against today's code, where the snap path has no way to express an explicit target and the unheld guard at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1963 returns before binding; also fails any 'fix' that opens the gate for all unheld callers, because row 2 still demands refusal.

testCases.name: testResumeRequestsMeshWhenTheCameraIsComingBack
testCases.asserts: On the extracted pure term: resumeReconstruction(supportsMesh: true, cameraIntended: true, pedestrian: true, thermalCritical: false) == true; resumeReconstruction(supportsMesh: true, cameraIntended: false, …) == false (warm-up resume still eats the idle diet — vacuity guard against a constant-true term); resumeReconstruction(supportsMesh: false, cameraIntended: true, …) == false and (…, thermalCritical: true) == false (the pre-existing conjuncts still bind). testCases.name: testHeldFlagCannotOutliveItsGesture
testCases.asserts: Sequence-drive the liveness reducer with Date arithmetic: begin(nearest: nil) → commit(resolved: nil) ⇒ held == false; begin(nearest: X) → captureCleared(reason: .removed) → tick(now: start+2s) ⇒ abandoned == true and held == false; and the STATE-L1 baseline still holds: begin(nearest: X) → tick(now: start+10s) with the finger down ⇒ abandoned == false (vacuity guard — a reducer that clears eagerly on every tick fails this row).
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today: path (a) returns from GeoARSessionManager.swift:1966 leaving the flag true, and path (b) is never re-examined because the expiry at :1150 is gated on editingDropID != nil, so `abandoned` never becomes true.

testCases.name: testSecondFingerSurvivesTheFirstCommit
testCases.asserts: begin(); begin(); commit() ⇒ gestureHeld == true (one finger is still down); then commit() ⇒ gestureHeld == false; and cancelLiveEdit() from any depth ⇒ gestureHeld == false with the counter floored at 0 (vacuity guard: a counter that never floors goes negative and a later begin/commit pair leaves it stuck true).
testCases.failsWhen: Fails today: the Bool at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1968 is cleared by the first commit, so row 1 comes back false and every subsequent tick from the still-live second gesture is refused at :1963.

The held-gesture immunity itself: a 10 s stationary hold no longer expires, and cancelLiveEdit clears the flag ahead of its own early-return guard (:461-462) — the round-2 wrong-drop-on-tick-silence path is genuinely closed.

reviews.lens: The three pure clocks and their CALLERS (staff Swift/AR seat). I traced each new predicate back to every state it reads and every call site that reaches it: markCameraHidden's stamp vs ARSessionHolder's pause scheduler (same t0?), passAttachedAt's stamping edges, resumeSession's session.run count on the three resume paths (hidden warm-up / visible warm resume / transit), and gestureAbandoned's thresholds vs the 400 ms tick and vs every non-gesture caller of adjustNearestDrop. Verdict: the three PREDICATES are correct, pure and non-vacuously tested — every escape in this diff is one layer out, in the caller state the new conjuncts are evaluated against. Two new conjuncts (`gestureHeld` in the re-bind refusal, `cameraVisible` in the resume plan) are each invariantly WRONG for one live call path: `gestureHeld` is invariantly false when "Place on ground" calls the commit (the feature is now a no-op), and `cameraVisible` is invariantly false at every resumeSession call site (the tab-return resume now fires two session.runs and drops the mesh). Same failure family the round-2 verdict named — a time/state-quantized coupling whose test hands the predicate a literal — moved from clocks to caller context. Code-side ruling only; the four empirical bars stay open on the owner's field runs.

closureVerdicts.item: STATE-L1 — gestureHeld liveness, pure gestureAbandoned, re-bind refusal, 30 s backstop
closureVerdicts.trace: BUILT AS SPECIFIED: beginLiveEdit() at GeoARSessionManager.swift:451-455 (sets gestureHeld, stamps lastLiveEditTickAt, captures editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id) wired to all three sliders' onEditingChanged(true) at ARScreen.swift:499-504, 526-531, 553-558; pure gestureAbandoned at :472-477 (held ? >30 : >1.5) consumed at :1150-1155; refusal at :1962-1965; commit clears gestureHeld at :1968 and editingDropID at :2041; cancelLiveEdit clears gestureHeld at :461 (before its guard, so it always clears). The round-2 defect is genuinely closed: a stationary finger can no longer expire, and updateNearest freezes at :1612 on editingDropID — so the capture now freezes nearest at touch-down instead of at the first value tick (a real improvement). PARTIAL because the refusal's blast radius was not bounded: it also gates the ONE non-gesture caller of adjustNearestDrop (snapNearestDropToGround at :2124), which has no beginLiveEdit — see F1 (CRITICAL). Residual: gestureHeld is not cleared where the capture is destroyed system-side (:1591, :890) — see F3.

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-R2-1 — true hide-edge stamp + pure cameraRecentlyVisible = pauseGrace + 1.0
closureVerdicts.trace: markCameraHidden stamps lastCameraVisibleAt at :574 AFTER cameraVisible = false at :569, so the per-tick stamp at :1156 can never overwrite the edge. Same t0 verified: ARSessionHolder.cameraDidDisappear calls markCameraHidden (line 70) then schedulePause (line 71), whose Task sleeps pauseGraceSeconds (line 113-115) — the pause fires at t0+5+ε, the grace releases at t0+6 (pure fn at :484-488, AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds = 5, AppConfig.swift:150). Margin 1.0 s > one 400 ms tick of jitter, and the plan's consumer at :1215-1216 OR's it with live cameraVisible. suspendSession (:423-444) cancels the tick loop, so no tick evaluates the window's tail; the appliedPerception reset at :438 leaves the stamp untouched, so a re-appear inside the window keeps the mesh request. No other reader of lastCameraVisibleAt exists. Test at WaveDTests.swift:425-441 is non-vacuous (reverting to `< pauseGraceSeconds` fails the pauseMoment assert at 5.0 < 5.0).

closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-LENS-1 — passShouldDetach(idle>5 && attached>10), both conjuncts bind
closureVerdicts.trace: Pure fn at :494-498; consumed at :1291-1294. passAttachedAt is stamped ONLY on the detached→attached edge (:1286-1288, guarded by !(semanticPass?.callbacksActive ?? false)), so attachedFor measures real dwell; passIdleSince nils on every needed tick (:1285) and arms one tick after work stops (:1298). Detach floor = max(idle 5 s, attach 10 s) ⇒ attach/detach cycles are ≥10 s apart, and for any pass attached ≥10 s the detach lands at ADR-035's measured 5 s idle (the pre-existing comment at :1270 states that number). Repeat detach calls are no-ops — SemanticOcclusionPass.setCallbacksActive guards on `changed` (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:184-195), so leaving passIdleSince armed after detach costs nothing. Test at WaveDTests.swift:443-455 is non-vacuous (the round-2 form fails the (6,11) assert).

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-R2-2 — resume plan carries the camera-visibility term (one run)
closureVerdicts.trace: The term is present (:545) and it DOES fix the scoped path: a warm-up resume with the camera hidden (ARSessionHolder.beginRevealWarmup → startIfNeeded line 104) now runs the idle diet once and the tick agrees (lastCameraVisibleAt stale ⇒ cameraRecentlyVisible false) — one run. But `cameraVisible` is INVARIANTLY FALSE at every resumeSession call site: resumeSession is reachable only via startIfNeeded's `else if !sessionRunning` (ARSessionHolder.swift:103-106), sessionRunning goes false only in suspend() (line 121-125), and suspendSession clears cameraVisible (:426); both restorers call manager.markCameraVisible() AFTER startIfNeeded (ARSessionHolder.swift:64-65 and :89-90). So the visible warm resume — camera tab return past the grace, and every foreground return — now resumes on the idle diet and the immediate first tick flips reconstruction back on: two session.runs and a mesh teardown+rebuild at the reveal moment. See F2 (HIGH). Also note the resume plan uses a different predicate than the tick (cameraVisible vs cameraVisible || cameraRecentlyVisible), which double-runs even the hidden path inside the 1 s [pause, grace-end] window.

findings.title: The re-bind refusal kills 'Place on ground': the only non-gesture caller is refused 100% of the time
findings.trace: adjustNearestDrop now opens with `if editingDropID == nil { guard gestureHeld else { return } … }` (:1962-1965). Callers are exactly seven (grep): six slider sites in ARScreen (each preceded by beginLiveEdit on onEditingChanged(true)) and ONE programmatic caller — snapNearestDropToGround at :2124, `adjustNearestDrop(height: min(max(targetHeight, -2), 20), commit: true)`, reached from the 'Place on ground' Button at ARScreen.swift:570-572. That path never calls beginLiveEdit. At button-tap time editingDropID is provably nil and gestureHeld provably false: editingDropID is set only in beginLiveEdit (:454) and the refusal branch (:1964), and is cleared on every commit (:2041), on vanish (:1975), by cancelLiveEdit (:464), removePerDropState (:1591) and resetPlacements (:890); gestureHeld is true only while a finger is down. So the guard returns, the height is NEVER applied, and control never reaches the commit block — no placedDrops write (:1984), no holder move (:1993), no library.update persist (:2032), no VPS anchor re-pin (:2046-2051), no groundLock clear (:2044). Execution then returns to :2126, which sets groundLockBaseY[drop.id] = groundY + 0.005 regardless. ARScreen's syncSliders() (:604-609) re-seeds from the unchanged nearestDrop, so the slider doesn't move either.
findings.harm: ADR-027's headline placement tool is dead on this build, 100% reproducible, and silent — the user taps 'Place on ground', nothing moves, no message appears (the decline path at :2111 is not even reached because groundY was measured successfully). Worse, the session is left inconsistent: groundLockBaseY is now authoritative in syncGPSPlacements (:1802, `let y = groundLockBaseY[drop.id] ?? …`) while drop.heightAboveGround still holds the old value and was never persisted — the drop may silently jump to the ground minutes later on the next drift sync, and returns to its old height on relaunch. A VPS-owned drop keeps its stale terrain anchor because the re-pin never fires. This is the exact 'field report 2026-07-07' re-float the ground lock exists to prevent.
findings.fix: Give the programmatic path an explicit capture instead of borrowing gesture state. Minimal and self-cleaning: insert `beginLiveEdit()` immediately before :2124 (it captures nearestDrop?.id and the following commit clears both flags at :1968/:2041). Structurally better: split capture-resolution from mutation — `private func applyAdjustment(id:height:scale:rotation:commit:)` called by both, with the gesture wrapper owning the refusal — so the refusal can never gate a non-gesture caller again.

findings.title: Resume's new cameraVisible conjunct is invariantly false at every call site — the visible warm resume now fires two session.runs and destroys the mesh
findings.trace: resumeSession is reachable from exactly one place: ARSessionHolder.startIfNeeded's `else if !sessionRunning { manager.resumeSession() }` (ARSessionHolder.swift:103-106). sessionRunning goes false only in suspend() (:121-125), which calls manager.suspendSession(), which clears cameraVisible (GeoARSessionManager.swift:426). Both visibility restorers run AFTER: cameraDidAppear does startIfNeeded() then markCameraVisible() (ARSessionHolder.swift:64-65); appDidBecomeActive does startIfNeeded() then markCameraVisible() (:89-90); beginRevealWarmup never restores it. So at every resumeSession invocation cameraVisible == false and the new conjunct at :545 forces resumePlan.reconstruction = false, appliedPerception = (false,false,false) (:551), and session.run with no sceneReconstruction (:552-556). startTicking (:563) then runs tick() immediately (:1044-1048, the loop body precedes the sleep) — by then markCameraVisible has already set cameraVisible = true, so perceptionPlan yields reconstruction = true (:1338-1341 with cameraRecentlyVisible true) and setPerception fires session.run #2 with .mesh (:852-865). Pre-diff (52786bf:489-491) the resume plan had no visibility term and matched the tick — exactly one run. Counted per the lens: (a) hidden warm-up resume = 1 run (the scoped fix works, except inside the 1 s [pause, grace-end] window where resume's `cameraVisible` and the tick's `cameraVisible || cameraRecentlyVisible` disagree ⇒ 2 runs); (b) visible warm resume = 2 runs (regression); (c) transit resume = 1 run.
findings.harm: Every camera-tab return past the 5 s grace and every foreground return after a call/app-switch now reconfigures the session twice within one runloop turn at the reveal moment — the precise defect round-2's ARPCFG-2 closed, and the comment claiming 'the common resume is exactly ONE run' (:538-539) is now false. Because run #1 requests no sceneReconstruction, ARKit drops the retained ARMeshAnchors that the warm resume exists to preserve, and run #2 rebuilds the mesh from nothing — the file's own contract at :721-723 ('every re-enable rebuilds the mesh from nothing, leaving a multi-second occlusion hole while sceneUnderstanding still requests occlusion'), with .occlusion still inserted (:1247-1253). That is seconds of real-geometry draw-over on the most common resume, against the wave's fourth bar, plus a double sessionRunSince stamp (:561, :864) delaying the ADR-043 reveal gate on the killer-#1 TTFO path.
findings.fix: Make the resume plan read the caller's truth, not a flag the caller restores afterwards. Either (a) reorder both restorers — markCameraVisible() BEFORE startIfNeeded() in cameraDidAppear and appDidBecomeActive (safe: markCameraVisible only sets the flag and the TTFO stamp), or (b) pass it explicitly: `manager.resumeSession(cameraVisible: cameraVisible)` from the holder, false from beginRevealWarmup. Then make the term identical to the tick's — `cameraVisible || Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(now: Date(), lastVisible: lastCameraVisibleAt)` — so the resume and the first tick can never disagree in the grace window.

findings.title: gestureHeld is not cleared where the capture is destroyed, disarming the re-bind refusal and stranding the 30 s backstop
findings.trace: The refusal at :1963 keys on gestureHeld alone, and gestureHeld is cleared in exactly two places: commit (:1968) and cancelLiveEdit (:461). The two system-side destroyers of the capture clear editingDropID but leave gestureHeld true: removePerDropState (:1591, `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }`, reached from syncGPSPlacements' removal loop :1855-1857 when the captured drop leaves eligibleDrops (:1568-1572) or is deleted, and from clearRoomDrops :669-671) and resetPlacements (:890, reached from runGPSCompass on a relocalization give-up :1066-1071 or a deferred failure recovery :1056-1061). In that state the 30 s lost-end backstop cannot fire either — updatePowerTier's expiry is guarded on `editingDropID != nil` (:1150) — so gestureHeld stays true until the next commit or cancelLiveEdit.
findings.harm: After a mid-drag removal or a mid-drag cold restart, the refusal — the mechanism STATE-L1 was built to provide — is off: any adjustNearestDrop tick that arrives without a fresh beginLiveEdit captures whatever nearestDrop is now (:1964) and a release-commit persists that value to the wrong drop, to disk and Firestore. Reachability is narrow in practice because the panel is hidden when nearestDrop goes nil (ARScreen.swift:289), which usually ends the drag; the certain part is the leaked flag: the refusal is disarmed and the backstop is unreachable for the rest of the session.
findings.fix: Clear the liveness where the capture dies: add `gestureHeld = false` next to :1591 and next to :890 (or route both through cancelLiveEdit). Optionally make the backstop independent of the capture — evaluate gestureAbandoned when `editingDropID != nil || gestureHeld` — so a lost end event always resolves.

testCases.name: testGroundSnapCommitsWithNoGestureInFlight (and a gesture tick with no capture is still refused)

findings.title: STATE-L1's re-bind refusal kills "Place on ground": every programmatic commit is now silently discarded
findings.trace: snapNearestDropToGround() (:2073) is reached from a plain Button — ARScreen.swift:570-572 — with no slider gesture in flight, so editingDropID is nil (cleared by the previous commit at :2041 or never set) and gestureHeld is false (cleared at :1968/:461). It measures the surface, then applies the result through adjustNearestDrop(height:commit:true) at :2124. The new refusal at :1962-1965 — `if editingDropID == nil { guard gestureHeld else { return } }` — returns before the identity resolve at :1966, so the entire body is skipped: holder.position.y is never moved (:1993), placedDrops/nearestDrop are never updated (:1984-1985), library.update(persist: true) is never called (:2030-2036), and groundLockBaseY[id] = nil (:2044) never runs. Control returns to :2126, which stamps groundLockBaseY[drop.id] = groundY + 0.005 anyway. Round-2 code had the unconditional `if editingDropID == nil { editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id }` and worked.
findings.harm: ADR-027's headline fix — the feature born of field report 2026-07-07 ("snap landed, then the geo pipeline lifted it again") — is a no-op on every tap. The object does not move, the slider readout does not change (syncSliders at ARScreen.swift:604 reads the unchanged nearestDrop), and heightAboveGround is never persisted to disk or Firestore. Worse, the orphaned ground lock at :2126 is still consulted by the compass re-sync (:1802) and the VPS terrain path (:931), so a geo-anchored drop is later dragged to the measured ground by a refinement tick while its stored height still says otherwise — the content silently reverts to the old height on the next launch or library sync. Room-mode drops (exempt from both positioners) never move at all. Ships as a dead button on a wave whose bar is crash-free/fps/thermal — no test covers it because the suite only tests pure predicates.
findings.fix: Give the programmatic caller a capture. Minimal and honest: in snapNearestDropToGround, immediately before :2124, set `editingDropID = drop.id` (the identity is already resolved and holder-validated at :2074-2075) — the commit path then clears it at :2041 exactly as a gesture commit does. Cleaner: add an explicit `programmatic: Bool = false` parameter to adjustNearestDrop and change the guard to `guard gestureHeld || programmatic else { return }`, so the refusal keeps meaning "a stale SLIDER tick" rather than "any caller without a finger". Audit any future non-gesture caller against the same rule.

findings.title: ARPCFG-R2-2's cameraVisible term is always false at resume — every warm resume now fires two session.run calls at the reveal moment
findings.trace: cameraDidAppear() runs startIfNeeded() (:64) → resumeSession() (:104) and only THEN manager.markCameraVisible() (:65). suspendSession already set cameraVisible = false (GeoARSessionManager.swift:426), so the new `&& cameraVisible` conjunct at :545 forces resumePlan.reconstruction = false; appliedPerception is stamped false (:551) and session.run issues the idle diet (:552-556). markCameraVisible then sets cameraVisible = true (:584). startTicking's Task (:1044-1049) is enqueued on the same MainActor and therefore runs only after cameraDidAppear returns, so its FIRST tick computes reconstruction = true (:1338-1341 via cameraVisible/cameraRecentlyVisible at :1214-1216), setPerception sees desired != appliedPerception (:854) and issues a second session.run milliseconds later. appDidBecomeActive() (:89-90) has the identical order. Pre-diff, resumePlan.reconstruction had no visibility term and matched the first tick, so the resume was one run — the exact ARPCFG-2 invariant the round-2 comment at :534-539 records.
findings.harm: Two configuration changes back-to-back at the reveal moment on LiDAR pedestrian hardware — the single instant Killer #1 (time-to-first-object) is measured. The first run tears mesh reconstruction out of the config (makeConfiguration :728-730), dropping the mesh anchors, and the second re-requests it, so meshing restarts from zero and sceneUnderstanding.occlusion (inserted unconditionally at :1252-1253 whenever capable) requests occlusion against a mesh that does not exist yet — the multi-second occlusion hole ADR-035/SWE-11 call out at :721-723, now on every tab return instead of never. Each run also re-negotiates the capture format (:759-786), a camera-stall and heat cost paid on the reveal frame. Field-visible as a hitch plus drawn-over content precisely when the user comes back to the camera; invisible to the suite because resumeSession is impure.
findings.fix: Swap the two statements in both lifecycle entry points: call `manager.markCameraVisible()` BEFORE `startIfNeeded()` in cameraDidAppear() (:64-65) and in appDidBecomeActive() (:89-90). markCameraVisible only writes cameraVisible/cameraVisibleAt/timeToFirstObjectMs (:583-592) and reads placedHolders, so it is safe before attach or resume, and it makes the TTFO stamp precede session bring-up (more honest for the metric too). Do not instead widen the term to cameraRecentlyVisible: on the real tab-return path the hide edge is already older than pauseGrace + 1.0 by the time suspend has fired and the user returns, so that term is false as well and the double run survives.

findings.title: Re-bind refusal does not cover a capture destroyed under a live finger — a drop deleted mid-drag re-binds the drag to a different drop
findings.trace: removePerDropState clears the capture (`if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil }`, :1591) but never touches gestureHeld (:249), so a finger still on the slider leaves gestureHeld == true with no capture. It also nils nearestDrop (:1598-1601), which protects only the first tick (the re-capture at :1964 yields nil and :1966 returns). But clearing editingDropID unfreezes updateNearest (:1612), so within one 400 ms tick nearestDrop is recomputed to a DIFFERENT drop; the next slider value tick then passes the refusal (editingDropID == nil, gestureHeld == true) and captures that drop at :1964. Subsequent ticks mutate it (:1984-1993) and the release commit persists it through library.update(persist: true) (:2030-2036). removePerDropState is called from the per-tick placement sync for any drop that leaves the library/render set (:1856, :2376) and from clearRoomDrops (:670), all reachable while a finger is down.
findings.harm: The precise failure STATE-L1's own docstring says was fixed (:241-248: "the still-live gesture re-bound to a DIFFERENT drop (a wrong-drop persist to disk and Firestore)") survives on the removal path: delete a drop remotely, or walk it out of the render set, while its height slider is under the user's thumb, and the drag silently continues on the neighbouring drop — height/scale/rotation are rewritten and, on release, persisted locally and pushed to Firestore against a drop the user never touched. Silent, data-corrupting, and not recoverable by undo. Narrower than the round-2 window (which needed only 1.5 s of tick silence), but the same harm class, and it is what makes the item PARTIAL rather than closed.
findings.fix: One line: inside the branch at :1591, kill the gesture with the capture — `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil; gestureHeld = false }`. The drag then refuses every further tick and the release commit (:1963), dying with the drop it was editing, which is the intended semantic; the next onEditingChanged(true) re-arms cleanly via beginLiveEdit (:451). Prefer a distinct `gestureBindingLost` flag over reusing gestureHeld only if a later feature needs to tell "finger down, target gone" from "no finger".

findings.title: The 30 s lost-end backstop stretches the nearest-freeze and the governor's .full pin from 1.5 s to 30 s
findings.trace: gestureAbandoned returns false for a held gesture until 30 s of tick silence (:476). While editingDropID is non-nil, updateNearest is frozen (:1612) and any drop already in liveEditingDrops keeps isLiveEditing true in the governor input (:1180), which pins the tier to .full. If the Slider view is destroyed mid-drag on a path that does not route through markCameraHidden (:568) or suspendSession (:423) — the only two callers of cancelLiveEdit — SwiftUI never delivers onEditingChanged(false), and both conditions now persist for 30 s instead of round 2's 1.5 s.
findings.harm: Up to 30 s of .full-tier perception (person segmentation at 14-29 ms/frame plus scene depth at 60 Hz internally) with no user interaction, plus a stale nearest-drop HUD, on a wave whose bar is thermal. Requires a lost end event AFTER at least one value tick (a purely stationary hold populates no liveEditingDrops), so the exposure is narrow and bounded — this is the trade the round-2 verdict explicitly ordered, recorded here as a known tail rather than a defect in the build.
findings.fix: No code change required for closure. If the tail is unwanted, cheapest mitigation is to release the governor pin earlier than the capture: in updatePowerTier, when gestureAbandoned(held: true) has not yet fired but silence exceeds ~2 s, clear liveEditingDrops (keeping editingDropID and gestureHeld) so the tier can fall while the binding is still held. Alternatively add .onDisappear { manager.cancelLiveEdit() } to adjustPanel (ARScreen.swift:592-601) so panel teardown becomes an explicit gesture end.

testCases.name: testProgrammaticCommitIsNeverRefused

reviews.lens: Swift + AR staff engineer, lens = the round-3 diff as a whole (git show HEAD, cf3d43d, 205 insertions across 5 files). Verified all seven scoped items plus the ride-along against source with file:line traces, then hunted blast radius on every changed line: beginLiveEdit's new call surface, gestureHeld's interaction with the roomDrops/demoDrops/ground-snap paths, the three sliders' onEditingChanged(true) wiring, markCameraHidden's double-stamp, the resumePlan's new cameraVisible conjunct against every resumeSession call site, and per-test vacuity of CallerClockTests against round-2 semantics. D4 applied: I looked for reasons NOT to file, and dropped two candidate items (the 5s-vs-15s detach toggle-rate tradeoff, which round 2 itself ordered and whose cycle floor is still the 10s attach dwell; and a VoiceOver-adjustable-slider path through the same new guard, which is unreachable today because the AR panel has zero accessibility affordances — 3 accessibilityLabels exist in the entire app, none on these sliders). Two findings survived, both genuinely introduced by this diff, both mechanically traceable, neither in the carried/deferred set.

closureVerdicts.item: STATE-L1 — gestureHeld liveness, pure gestureAbandoned, re-bind refusal, 30s backstop
closureVerdicts.trace: BUILT AS SPECIFIED for the slider seam: gestureHeld declared GeoARSessionManager.swift:249; beginLiveEdit() at :451-455 (sets held, stamps lastLiveEditTickAt, captures editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id); wired to all three sliders' onEditingChanged(true) at ARScreen.swift:499-504 (height), :526-531 (scale), :553-558 (rotation); pure gestureAbandoned(now:lastTick:held:) at :472-477 (held ? >30 : >1.5); driven from updatePowerTier at :1150-1155; cancelLiveEdit clears held at :461 BEFORE its early-return guard at :462 (correct — held is cleared even with no capture); commit clears held at :1968. Ordering is sound: onEditingChanged(true) fires before the binding's first set, and adjustPanel only renders when nearestDrop != nil (ARScreen.swift:289), so beginLiveEdit's capture never comes up empty. HOLE: the re-bind refusal at :1962-1965 is a blanket guard on adjustNearestDrop, and the manager's OWN internal commit — snapNearestDropToGround at :2124 — reaches it with editingDropID == nil and gestureHeld == false. See finding WD3-1. Closed on the seam it was scoped to; opened a critical hole one call site over.

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-R2-1 — true hide-edge stamp + pure cameraRecentlyVisible
closureVerdicts.trace: markCameraHidden stamps lastCameraVisibleAt = Date() at GeoARSessionManager.swift:574, at the true edge (immediately after cameraVisible = false at :569). Pure cameraRecentlyVisible(now:lastVisible:) at :484-488 = pauseGraceSeconds + 1.0 (5 + 1 = 6s), consumed at :1216. Per-tick stamp retained at :1156 for the visible case. DOUBLE-STAMP CHECK (lens item): markCameraHidden has exactly one caller, ARSessionHolder.cameraDidDisappear:68-72, which in the same call also re-arms schedulePause (:71 → :109-119, a fresh 5s pause task). ARScreen can fire cameraDidDisappear twice on a cover dismissal (onDisappear:83 plus onChange(of: isActive):89), but each repeat restarts the grace AND the pause in lockstep, so the 6s grace can never be extended relative to the 5s pause it exists to outlast. No path extends grace alone. Clean.

closureVerdicts.item: RENDER-LENS-1 — passShouldDetach, both conjuncts bind
closureVerdicts.trace: Pure passShouldDetach(idleFor:attachedFor:) at GeoARSessionManager.swift:494-498 = idleFor > 5 && attachedFor > 10; driven at :1291-1294 from passIdleSince (:1285, :1298) and passAttachedAt (:1287, stamped only on a genuine off→on edge via the callbacksActive check at :1286). That is exactly the trade round 2's own verdict ordered, and 5s matches ADR-035's measured idle window; not re-litigated.

closureVerdicts.item: ARPCFG-R2-2 — resume plan carries the camera-visibility term
closureVerdicts.trace: The term is present — GeoARSessionManager.swift:545 adds `&& cameraVisible` to resumePlan.reconstruction (:543-550) — but it is invariantly FALSE at every entry into resumeSession, so the reconstruction axis of the resume plan is now dead. cameraVisible is written in exactly four places (:140 init false, :426 suspendSession false, :569 markCameraHidden false, :584 markCameraVisible true). resumeSession is reached only via ARSessionHolder.startIfNeeded:103-105, whose three callers all set visibility AFTER the call: cameraDidAppear (:64 startIfNeeded, :65 markCameraVisible), appDidBecomeActive (:89, :90), and beginRevealWarmup (:57, never marks visible). Correct as scoped. Downstream note, not a defect of this item: because WD3-1 makes the SUCCESS path of snapNearestDropToGround a silent no-op, this decline toast is currently the only observable outcome the button can produce.

closureVerdicts.trace: PersonSentinel.swift:49 captures holdStart BEFORE queue.async at :50, after the busy/rate gate releases the lock at :43 — so the enqueue-to-execute wait is inside the measured hold, which is the thermal failure mode the instrument exists to catch. Throttle at :56-64: lastLongHoldLogAt (:21) seeded .distantPast so the first long hold always logs; shouldLog = held > 0.1 && now - lastLongHoldLogAt > 60; both the read and the write happen inside lock.lock()/unlock() (:57-62) and the os_log call is outside the lock. Never latches off — a sustained sawtooth reports once a minute forever. Log text updated to say 'incl. queue wait' (:64), so the field trace can't be misread.

closureVerdicts.trace: GeoARSessionManager.swift:2496-2503: the USE gate now calls Self.midFieldServiceable(distance:) (:1364-1367), the same predicate perceptionPlan's request side uses at :1354, and carries ARWorldTrackingConfiguration.supportsFrameSemantics(.sceneDepth) at :2498; the inline maxServiceable duplicate is gone. Outer gate at :2482 still carries AppConfig.midFieldDepthEnabled, so the request/use flag symmetry holds. The doc comment at :1360-1363 claiming ONE shared predicate is now true rather than aspirational — that is the 'false sharing comment corrected' item. That is now impossible.

closureVerdicts.item: CallerClockTests — vacuity check, per test, against ROUND-2 code
closureVerdicts.trace: All three discriminate; per-test answer. (1) testHeldGestureIsNeverAbandonedByTickSilence (WaveDTests.swift:386-403): assert 1 (held, +10s → expect false) FAILS under round-2 semantics (`silent > 1.5` with no held term → true). Discriminating. Residual gap, not filed: the 30s backstop is pinned only from above (+31 → true), so a mutation to `held ? silent > 20` still passes — add a (+29, held) → false row. (2) testVisibilityGraceStrictlyOutlastsThePause (:405-421): asserts 1 (+5.0) and 2 (+5.4) both FAIL under round-2's `< pauseGraceSeconds`; assert 3 (+6.5 → false) pins the upper bound and kills a `+5.0` mutation. Both boundaries pinned — the strongest of the three. (3) testPassDetachBothConjunctsBind (:423-435): assert 3 (idle 6, attached 11 → expect true) FAILS under round-2's `idle > 15`. Discriminating. Asserts 1 and 2 agree with round 2 but each independently pins one round-3 conjunct against mutation. Statics are `nonisolated static` on a @MainActor class and AppConfig is a plain enum, so the non-isolated XCTestCase call sites compile. COVERAGE GAP that let both findings through: no test in the suite touches adjustNearestDrop, snapNearestDropToGround, or the resume plan (`grep -rn 'adjustNearestDrop|snapNearest|beginLiveEdit' AugmentMeRealityTests/` returns nothing) — the two seams that broke are the two seams with no test.

findings.title: STATE-L1's re-bind refusal also refuses the manager's own ground-snap commit — "Place on ground" (ADR-027) is now a silent no-op
findings.trace: The new guard `guard gestureHeld else { return }` at :1963 fires for ANY caller of adjustNearestDrop that arrives with editingDropID == nil, not just stale slider ticks. snapNearestDropToGround is such a caller: it measures the surface through the truth chain (:2079-2105) and then commits the result with `adjustNearestDrop(height:..., commit: true)` at :2124. At that moment editingDropID is nil (it is written only by beginLiveEdit at :454 and cleared by the previous commit at :2041 / cancelLiveEdit at :464) and gestureHeld is false (set true only by beginLiveEdit at :452 on a slider touch-down, cleared on every commit at :1968). The button is a plain SwiftUI Button (ARScreen.swift:570-572) — no slider is held when it is tapped. So :1963 returns and the height is never applied, never written to placedDrops, never persisted. Execution then resumes at :2126, which still writes `groundLockBaseY[drop.id] = groundY + 0.005`. Only editingDropID != nil (a slider gesture whose end callback was lost, inside the new 30s backstop) lets the snap through — the feature now works only when a gesture is broken. Verified reachable: adjustPanel renders whenever nearestDrop != nil && renderedDropCount > 0 (ARScreen.swift:289), and snapNearestDropToGround's own guards (:2074-2075) are satisfied in exactly that state. Round-2 code had `if editingDropID == nil { editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id }` unconditionally, so the snap worked; this commit is what broke it.
findings.harm: ADR-027's ground lock — the fix for field report 2026-07-07 ("snap landed, then the geo pipeline lifted it again") — is dead. Tapping "Place on ground" moves nothing, shows no toast (the UX-3 decline at :2115 only fires when the raycast chain misses), and persists nothing: the library.update at :2030-2036 is never reached, so the corrected height never reaches disk or Firestore and is gone on relaunch. Worse, the stale write at :2126 leaves groundLockBaseY set to the measured ground for a drop whose heightAboveGround was never changed, and that lock is authoritative downstream — it overrides the VPS transform's Y at :931-933 and wins outright over the computed height in the compass placement at :1802-1803. Result: the content silently teleports to ground on some later re-sync while the persisted model still says it floats, and the commit's own lock-clearing path (:2044) never runs to undo it. This is the placement-correctness killer the wave exists to protect, reachable by one tap on the primary adjust panel.
findings.fix: Give the authored internal commit its own capture instead of borrowing a gesture's. Minimal: in snapNearestDropToGround, set `editingDropID = drop.id` immediately before the call at :2124 (the drop identity is already resolved and guarded at :2074) — the commit path at :2039-2041 clears it again. Cleaner and self-documenting: add `targetID: UUID? = nil` to adjustNearestDrop and have :1962 read `if editingDropID == nil { if let targetID { editingDropID = targetID } else { guard gestureHeld else { return }; editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id } }`, with :2124 passing `targetID: drop.id`. Either way the STATE-L1 refusal is preserved for its actual target (a slider tick with no capture and no held finger). While in the function, also hoist `if commit { gestureHeld = false }` (:1968) above the `guard let id` at :1966 so a commit that finds no target still releases the liveness flag.

findings.title: The resume plan's new `&& cameraVisible` conjunct is invariantly false at every call site — every warm resume now runs the no-mesh config and fires a second session.run one tick later
findings.trace: cameraVisible is written in exactly four places: :140 (init false), :426 (suspendSession false), :569 (markCameraHidden false), :584 (markCameraVisible true). resumeSession (:509-564) is reached only through ARSessionHolder.startIfNeeded:103-105, and all three of its callers set visibility AFTER that call — cameraDidAppear does startIfNeeded at ARSessionHolder.swift:64 then markCameraVisible at :65; appDidBecomeActive does :89 then :90; beginRevealWarmup (:57) never marks visible at all. suspendSession has already forced cameraVisible false at :426, and resumeSession is only invoked when sessionRunning is false, i.e. after a suspend. So at :545 cameraVisible is false 100% of the time and resumePlan.reconstruction (:543-550) is now permanently false — the identical dead-conjunct shape RENDER-LENS-1 was raised to kill, reintroduced one function away. Consequence chain: appliedPerception is set to (false, false, false) at :551 and session.run executes the no-mesh configuration at :552-556. ~400ms later (tick loop, :1042-1048) updatePowerTier runs with cameraVisible now true, stamps lastCameraVisibleAt at :1156, so perceptionPlan's cameraRecentlyVisible term (:1215-1216) is true and plan.reconstruction (:1338-1341) is true on any mesh-capable pedestrian device below thermal-critical. setPerception (:852-866) sees the tuple differ and issues a SECOND session.run. Round-2 code had no cameraVisible term on the resume plan, so resume and first tick agreed and the resume was exactly one run — the invariant ARPCFG-2's own comment at :534-539 states.
findings.harm: Every return to the camera after the 5s pause grace (ARSessionHolder schedulePause:109-119 → suspend) now reconfigures ARKit twice within 400ms, and the first of those two configurations has scene reconstruction OFF. Disabling and re-enabling sceneReconstruction discards the ARMeshAnchors and restarts meshing from scratch — the multi-second occlusion hole the code itself names at :1308 ("rebuilds leave multi-second occlusion holes") and precisely the destroy-and-rebuild that round 2's ARPCFG-4 grace window exists to prevent. The hole lands in the worst possible window: the first seconds after the user re-opens the camera, when they are looking straight at the content. Content draws over real geometry during the rebuild — the wave's draw-over bar — plus a wasted reconfiguration's worth of CPU/GPU against the fps and thermal bars, on the single most common resume path in the app. The one case the conjunct was meant to serve (beginRevealWarmup, camera genuinely hidden) is also the one case where markCameraVisible is never called, so it would be served correctly by any fix.
findings.fix: Fix the ordering at the seam, which restores the term's intended meaning rather than deleting it: in ARSessionHolder, move `manager.markCameraVisible()` to BEFORE `startIfNeeded()` in cameraDidAppear (swap :64/:65) and in appDidBecomeActive (swap :89/:90). beginRevealWarmup is untouched and still resumes with cameraVisible false, so the warm-up resume keeps the idle diet exactly as ARPCFG-R2-2 intended. Belt-and-braces: make the resume plan and the tick plan share one predicate rather than two hand-written copies — extract the reconstruction term used at :1338-1341 into a nonisolated static and call it from both :543-550 and perceptionPlan, so no future edit can make the two disagree again.

testCases.name: testAuthoredCommitBindsWithoutAHeldGesture
testCases.asserts: Extract the capture decision as a pure static in the caller-clock style the round-2 verdict demanded: `nonisolated static func liveEditTarget(capture: UUID?, authored: UUID?, gestureHeld: Bool, nearest: UUID?) -> UUID?`, called from adjustNearestDrop's :1962 block. Three rows: (capture: nil, authored: A, held: false, nearest: A) -> A — an authored internal commit binds with no finger down; (capture: nil, authored: nil, held: false, nearest: A) -> nil — a slider tick with no capture and no held gesture is still refused; (capture: B, authored: nil, held: true, nearest: A) -> B — an existing capture always beats current nearest.
testCases.failsWhen: Vacuity-proofed in BOTH directions. Row 1 fails against HEAD (the guard at :1963 returns, so the target is nil and "Place on ground" is a no-op). Row 2 fails against round-2 code (unconditional `editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id` yields A, resurrecting the STATE-L1 wrong-drop persist). Row 3 fails against any fix that lets an authored target override a live gesture's capture. No single-line mutation of the predicate passes all three.

testCases.name: FT-GROUND-SNAP — field case: place, float, snap, relaunch
testCases.asserts: On device: place a drop, raise it with the height slider and release, tap "Place on ground" once with no slider touched. Assert (a) the content visibly drops to the measured surface within one frame, (b) the height readout in adjustPanel changes after syncSliders (ARScreen.swift:572), (c) no persist-error toast appears, and (d) after force-quit and relaunch the drop is still on the ground — i.e. library.update(persist: true) actually ran.
testCases.failsWhen: Fails against HEAD on all four assertions: the tap produces no movement, no readout change, no toast, and nothing persisted — while groundLockBaseY (:2126) is silently written, so (d) can additionally show the drop snapping to ground later in the SAME session and floating again after relaunch. This is the assertion set that would have caught the regression; no automated test in the suite touches this path today.

testCases.name: testResumePlanAgreesWithTheFirstTickPlan
testCases.asserts: Extract the resume reconstruction term as `nonisolated static func resumeReconstruction(supportsMesh:cameraVisible:pedestrian:thermalCritical:)` and assert, over the full 2^4 fact table, that it equals `perceptionPlan(...).reconstruction` fed the identical facts. The load-bearing row is (supportsMesh: true, camera visible at resume: true, pedestrian: true, thermalCritical: false) -> both sides TRUE, so resume and the first tick request the same configuration and the resume is exactly one session.run.
