verdicts.findingId: F-D3-01 / R3-1 (reviewer-2) / R3-1 (reviewer-3) / WD3-1 — "Place on ground" killed by the re-bind refusal
verdicts.reasoning: Verified by execution of the whole chain, not by reading. (1) Repo-wide grep for `adjustNearestDrop` returns exactly 7 call sites: ARScreen.swift:494/506/521/533/548/560 (the three sliders, each preceded by beginLiveEdit on onEditingChanged(true) at :504/:531/:558) and GeoARSessionManager.swift:2124 inside snapNearestDropToGround. (2) `gestureHeld` has exactly two setters-to-true — none (only beginLiveEdit:452) — and is cleared at :1968 (every commit) and :461 (cancelLiveEdit). (3) `editingDropID` is written only at :454, :1964 and cleared at :890, :1591, :1975, :2041, :464. (4) snapNearestDropToGround is reached from a plain SwiftUI Button (ARScreen.swift:570-572) with no slider touch, so at :2124 both editingDropID == nil and gestureHeld == false, and `guard gestureHeld else { return }` at :1963 returns before ANY mutation — before the identity resolve at :1966, the model write at :1984, the holder move at :1993, the library.update(persist: true) at :2030-2036, the groundLock clear at :2044 and the VPS re-pin at :2046-2051. All four reviewers traced this identically and all four are right. The harm chain is worse than a dead button and I verified the downstream half independently: control returns to :2126 which stamps `groundLockBaseY[drop.id] = groundY + 0.005` regardless, and that lock is authoritative in two places — it overwrites the VPS transform's Y at :931-933 and wins outright over the computed height at :1802 (`groundLockBaseY[drop.id] ?? min(max(groundY + ... )))`). syncGPSPlacements(animated: true) fires on the refinement path at :1751 behind an 8 s refractory plus correction/heading thresholds, so the drop is dragged to the measured ground at a later, non-deterministic moment while drop.heightAboveGround still holds the old value and was never persisted. Net user-visible sequence: tap does nothing → no toast (the :2115 decline is not reached, groundY was measured successfully) → the object moves on its own minutes later → it is back at the old height after relaunch. This is a regression introduced by cf3d43d: pre-diff the line was the unconditional `if editingDropID == nil { editingDropID = nearestDrop?.id }`. It is squarely the placement-correctness killer (ADR-027, field report 2026-07-07) that this wave exists to protect, reachable by one tap on the primary adjust panel. Severity CRITICAL is correct. Not carried, not deferred, not manufactured.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Reject the two minimal fixes on offer. Reviewer-3's `editingDropID = drop.id` before :2124 works today only because editingDropID and nearestDrop provably track each other (beginLiveEdit captures nearestDrop?.id and :1985 keeps writing nearestDrop = drop) — it silently clobbers a live capture the moment that invariant is edited, and the commit at :1968 still clears gestureHeld out from under any finger still down (that is F-D3-04's shape). Reviewer-4's `targetID:` parameter is better but leaves the gesture rules and the mutation in one function. The house already has the right pattern one screen away: relocateNearestDrop (:2158-2227) is an authored, non-gesture edit and it writes model + scene + cloud directly (:2197-2226) without touching the gesture capture at all. Follow it. Split adjustNearestDrop at line 1966: `private func applyEdit(to id: UUID, height: Double?, scale: Double?, rotation: Double?, commit: Bool)` holds everything from :1966 onward; `adjustNearestDrop(...)` becomes the gesture wrapper that resolves the id under the gesture rules and delegates; `snapNearestDropToGround` calls `applyEdit(to: drop.id, height: ..., commit: true)` with the id it already resolved and holder-validated at :2074. Then expose the binding decision as a pure `nonisolated static func editTarget(capture: UUID?, held: Bool, authored: UUID?, nearest: UUID?) -> UUID?` and table-test it — the caller-clock rule the round-2 verdict imposed on clocks, applied to caller CONTEXT, which is where both round-3 escapes actually live. The test must be two-directional (authored binds with no finger; an unheld tick with no capture is still refused; a live capture is never overridden), so neither deleting the guard nor opening it for all unheld callers can pass.

verdicts.findingId: F-D3-02 / R3-2 (reviewer-2) / R3-2 (reviewer-3) / WD3-2 — the resume plan's new `&& cameraVisible` conjunct is invariantly false
verdicts.reasoning: Verified exhaustively by grep over every lifecycle entry point, not by argument. `markCameraVisible` has exactly two call sites in the whole app — ARSessionHolder.swift:65 and :90 — and BOTH run after `startIfNeeded()` (:64 and :89). `resumeSession` has exactly one call site, ARSessionHolder.swift:104, inside `else if !sessionRunning`. `sessionRunning` goes false only in suspend():124, which calls manager.suspendSession(), which sets cameraVisible = false at GeoARSessionManager.swift:426. The third entry, beginRevealWarmup (ARSessionHolder.swift:55-59, called from ReceiveScreen.swift:50 and OnboardingView.swift:154), never marks visible at all. Therefore at GeoARSessionManager.swift:545 `cameraVisible` is false on 100% of reachable executions and resumePlan.reconstruction is permanently false — the identical dead-conjunct shape RENDER-LENS-1 was raised to kill, reintroduced 50 lines away in the same commit. Consequence verified line by line: appliedPerception is stamped (false,false,false) at :551, session.run executes a configuration with no sceneReconstruction at :552-556 (makeConfiguration:728-730 only sets .mesh when the flag is true), startTicking at :563 enqueues a Task whose loop body calls tick() BEFORE its first sleep (:1044-1048), tick reaches updatePowerTier unconditionally at :1079 (the only guard, :1075, is !isInterrupted/!sessionFailed), and by then markCameraVisible has already run synchronously, so perceptionPlan yields reconstruction = true (:1338-1341) and setPerception fires a second arView.session.run at :856. Pre-diff the resume plan had no visibility term and agreed with the tick — one run, which is exactly what the surviving comment at :534-539 still claims. Two harms, both against this wave's own bars. First, the wasted reconfiguration lands at the reveal instant and stamps sessionRunSince twice (:561 and :864), re-arming the ADR-043 reveal gate on the killer-#1 TTFO path. Second and worse, run #1 strips sceneReconstruction: the file's own recorded measurement at :721-723 says every re-enable rebuilds the mesh from nothing and leaves a multi-second occlusion hole while sceneUnderstanding still requests occlusion — and .occlusion is inserted at :823 and re-derived every tick. So every camera-tab return past the 5 s grace and every foreground return after a call now buys seconds of content drawing over real geometry, which IS the wave's fourth bar. HIGH is correct.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Do the call-order fix AND the shared-predicate fix; either alone leaves a hole. (a) Move `manager.markCameraVisible()` above `startIfNeeded()` in cameraDidAppear (ARSessionHolder.swift:64-65) and appDidBecomeActive (:89-90). markCameraVisible (:583-592) only writes cameraVisible/cameraVisibleAt/timeToFirstObjectMs and reads placedHolders, so it is safe before session bring-up, and it makes the TTFO stamp precede the run — more honest for the metric. Reviewer-3 is right that widening the resume term to cameraRecentlyVisible alone does not fix the tab-return path. (b) But reviewer-4 is right that the deeper defect is two hand-written copies of one decision: even after (a), beginRevealWarmup resuming inside the [pause, grace-end] window still computes resume=false / tick=true and double-runs (see my OWN-3). Extract `nonisolated static func reconstructionDesired(supportsMesh: Bool, cameraVisibleOrRecent: Bool, pedestrian: Bool, thermalCritical: Bool) -> Bool` and call it from BOTH :543-550 and perceptionPlan:1338-1341, with the visibility argument supplied as the caller's intent rather than read from a flag the caller restores one statement later. Then the resume and the first tick are incapable of disagreeing, and the full truth table is table-testable. Reviewer-2's `resumeSession(cameraIntended:)` signature is the right plumbing for the argument.

verdicts.findingId: F-D3-03 / R3-3 (reviewer-2) / R3-3 (reviewer-3) — gestureHeld outlives its gesture
verdicts.reasoning: The state leak is CONFIRMED; the data-corruption harm reviewer-3 attached to it (HIGH, wrong-drop persist to Firestore) is NOT demonstrated, and reviewer-2's LOW is the closest calibration. Confirmed half: gestureHeld is cleared in exactly two places — commit at :1968 and cancelLiveEdit at :461 — and there are two reachable ways to strand it true. (i) removePerDropState:1591 clears editingDropID but never touches gestureHeld, so a system-side destruction of the capture (reached from the placement-sync removal loop and clearRoomDrops) leaves held == true with no capture. (ii) The clear at :1968 sits BELOW the `guard let id = editingDropID else { return }` at :1966, so a commit that resolves no target returns with the flag still set. In that state the expiry can never re-examine it, because updatePowerTier's abandonment check at :1150 is gated on `editingDropID != nil` — so the flag persists until the next commit, markCameraHidden:578 or suspendSession:441. That is a genuine hygiene defect introduced by this diff and it is one line to fix. Refuted half: reviewer-3 claims the still-live drag then re-binds to a different drop and persists to disk and Firestore. Walking the same path, removePerDropState nils nearestDrop in the same call (:1598-1601) whenever the removed drop was nearest — and editingDropID and nearestDrop provably track each other (beginLiveEdit captures nearestDrop?.id; :1985 rewrites nearestDrop = drop), so they are always the same id at removal time. The adjust panel is gated on `manager.nearestDrop != nil` (ARScreen.swift:289), so the Slider is torn down at the next SwiftUI render pass, which is orders of magnitude sooner than the 400 ms tick that would have to run updateNearest to re-point nearestDrop at a different drop. There is therefore no window in which a surviving Slider delivers a tick while nearestDrop names a drop the user was not editing. What IS certain is the leak plus one behavioural absurdity it creates in combination with the CRITICAL: while the flag is latched, "Place on ground" works; while it is not, the same tap does nothing — the same button has two outcomes depending on invisible history. I rate the composite LOW-MEDIUM. It is not independently ship-blocking, but it costs three lines and it is in the same function as the CRITICAL fix, so it ships with it.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Three lines, all in the round-4 spot fix. (1) Kill the liveness where the capture dies: `if editingDropID == id { editingDropID = nil; gestureHeld = false }` at :1591 (and the same at resetPlacements:890, or route both through cancelLiveEdit). (2) Hoist the commit clear above the resolve guard — move `if commit { gestureHeld = false }` from :1968 to before :1966 — so a commit that finds no target still releases the flag. (3) Make the backstop reachable whenever any gesture state is outstanding: change :1150 from `if editingDropID != nil` to `if editingDropID != nil || gestureHeld`, so a lost end event always resolves instead of depending on a capture that may already be gone. All three are testable off the MainActor once the liveness is a small reducer rather than two raw fields, which is the same extraction F-D3-01's fix requires — do them as one change, not four.

verdicts.findingId: F-D3-04 — multi-slider hand-off: committing one slider kills a still-live drag on another
verdicts.reasoning: The code trace is exactly right and I confirmed every line of it; the severity is not. Confirmed: gestureHeld is a single Bool (GeoARSessionManager.swift:249) shared by three independently draggable Sliders (ARScreen.swift:489, :516, :543 — three separate views, and UIControl's isExclusiveTouch defaults to false, so nothing in UIKit stops two of them tracking two fingers). The sequence resolves as filed: finger A's commit sets gestureHeld = false at :1968 and editingDropID = nil at :2041, after which every remaining tick from finger B hits :1962 with no capture and :1963 with held false and is refused — including B's own release commit. The HUD keeps moving because liveScale is @State (ARScreen.swift:519-520) while the AR content and the model do not, so the slider appears to stop working until the user lifts and re-grabs. It is a real regression of this diff: the pre-diff unconditional capture kept B's ticks binding. Where I depart from reviewer-1's MEDIUM: this needs a deliberate two-finger operation on a compact HUD panel that also carries a 60 m-away drop's guidance card, and I did not execute it on device — SwiftUI's own gesture arbitration between sibling Sliders is not something I am willing to assert from the source alone. It is a LOW, and more usefully it is a SYMPTOM: the root cause is one Bool asked to answer two different questions ("is any gesture live?" and "is this caller authorized to bind?"), which is the same root cause as the CRITICAL and as the leak. Fixing the root cause fixes all three; filing it as its own round would be padding. Not independently ship-blocking.
verdicts.industrialSolution: Model liveness as gesture DEPTH, not a boolean, as reviewer-1 prescribed: `private var heldGestures = 0`; beginLiveEdit increments; commit does `heldGestures = max(0, heldGestures - 1)`; cancelLiveEdit zeroes it; `gestureHeld` becomes the computed `heldGestures > 0`. Keep editingDropID as the single shared capture — two fingers on one panel are editing one drop, which is the correct semantics. The floor at zero is load-bearing and must be asserted: an unfloored counter goes negative on an unpaired commit and then latches true forever. Feed the counter through the same pure `gestureAbandoned(now:lastTick:held:)` so the round-2 caller-clock rule survives. Add one 30-second device check to the field list (two thumbs, height and size simultaneously, release height first) to convert my LOW from inference to measurement — that is cheaper than another review round.

verdicts.findingId: R3-4 (reviewer-3) — the 30 s backstop stretches the nearest-freeze and the governor's .full pin from 1.5 s to 30 s
verdicts.reasoning: Refuted as a FINDING, not as an observation — and the filing reviewer says so himself: "No code change required for closure... recorded here as a known tail rather than a defect in the build." That makes it a priced tradeoff, and D5 puts priced tradeoffs the counsel itself ordered outside the finding set. Two substantive reasons beyond the label. First, the 30 s backstop is precisely what the round-2 verdict commissioned in STATE-L1 — re-pricing it now is re-litigation of a settled decision, which DECISIONS.md forbids. Second, the worst leg of the claimed harm does not connect: the .full pin requires `!liveEditingDrops.isEmpty` (PowerGovernor input at :1180), and the dominant path to a lost end event is removePerDropState, which removes the id from liveEditingDrops at :1590 in the same call — so the governor falls even while gestureHeld is stranded. What remains is a stale nearest-drop freeze on a narrow path, bounded at 30 s, requiring a lost end event after at least one value tick. Recording it as a Wave E tail is correct; filing it against a 200-line closure diff is not.
verdicts.industrialSolution: None required for closure. If the tail is ever unwanted, the cheapest correct mitigation is the one already named: release the governor pin earlier than the capture — clear liveEditingDrops at ~2 s of silence while keeping editingDropID and the held flag — so the tier can fall while the binding still holds. The `.onDisappear { manager.cancelLiveEdit() }` alternative on adjustPanel (ARScreen.swift:592) is tempting and should be resisted: onDisappear also fires on ordinary panel churn and would convert legitimate hidden-but-live states into cancellations. Carry to Wave E with STATE-L2/L3/L5.

ownFindings.title: Wave D's stated exit condition is not executable: Thread Sanitizer does not exist for physical iOS devices — the "on-device TSan run" can never be run, on this build or any other
ownFindings.trace: Verified on this machine, not recalled. Xcode 26.6 (17F113). `ls /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Toolchains/XcodeDefault.xctoolchain/usr/lib/clang/*/lib/darwin/ | grep tsan` returns exactly: libclang_rt.tsan_iossim_dynamic.dylib, tsan_osx_dynamic, tsan_tvossim_dynamic, tsan_watchossim_dynamic, tsan_xros_dynamic, tsan_xrossim_dynamic. There is NO libclang_rt.tsan_ios_dynamic.dylib — the runtime Apple ships for TSan covers macOS, visionOS and the SIMULATORS only. The same directory does contain libclang_rt.asan_ios_dynamic.dylib and libclang_rt.ubsan_ios_dynamic.dylib, and /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/usr/lib/libMainThreadChecker.dylib exists — so ASan, UBSan and Main Thread Checker DO run on the iPhone; TSan does not, and its checkbox greys out on a device destination. This matters because the race RENDER-1 named is not app-side state: SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:197-205 assigns `arView.renderCallbacks.prepareWithDevice` and `.postProcess` OUTSIDE stateLock (the lock is taken at :185 and released at :194, before the guard at :195), while RealityKit's render thread reads and invokes those slots from a thread the app does not own. No app-side lock can synchronize the read side, and no available tool can instrument that thread on device. The round-2 verdict made this a wave-exit condition and round 3 built the dwell floor as "step 1" with "step 2, the on-device TSan run, is a field task" (comment at GeoARSessionManager.swift:1282-1283) — that field task cannot be performed.
ownFindings.harm: Wave D would either be held open forever waiting on an impossible task, or — worse — closed by someone recording an unexecuted step as done. Either way the 99.5% crash-free bar gets signed on a false premise: the counsel's own record says RENDER-1 "needs the detach dwell floor + a TSan device run before the 99.5% crash bar is signable," and half of that sentence is unsatisfiable. This is exactly the failure the BRIEF forbids ("Measure, then claim"), and it would land in DECISIONS.md as law.
ownFindings.fix: Amend the exit condition in DECISIONS.md to what is actually dischargeable, and record why. Substitute protocol, all four legs required: (1) the dwell floor — shipped in round 3, both conjuncts binding, verified; (2) a Simulator TSan run of the test target — I verified this project builds and links under TSan today: `xcodebuild -project AugmentMeReality.xcodeproj -scheme AugmentMeReality -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 17 Pro' -enableThreadSanitizer YES CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO build-for-testing` → ** TEST BUILD SUCCEEDED **; add one test that drives SemanticOcclusionPass.setCallbacksActive from a background queue against a reader loop hammering `callbacksActive`, which is the part of the surface TSan CAN see; (3) an ASan + UBSan + Main Thread Checker device session across a 10-minute engaged run — these cover the use-after-free and main-thread-violation half of the same surface and DO run on the iPhone; (4) zero crash reports over FT-28 + FT-31, checked in Settings → Privacy & Security → Analytics & Improvements → Analytics Data. State plainly in the ADR that the RealityKit render-thread slot assignment remains formally unverified by tooling and is mitigated, not proven, by the dwell floor — a one-line honest unknown is worth more than a checkbox.

ownFindings.title: The instrument round 3 fixed FIRST so the field runs could attribute heat is invisible to the field run's own log filter — PersonSentinel's os_log carries no subsystem or category
ownFindings.trace: PersonSentinel.swift:64 calls the free function `os_log(.error, "PersonSentinel buffer hold exceeded 100 ms (%.0f ms incl. queue wait) — capture pool under pressure", held * 1000)`. With no log handle, that call uses OS_LOG_DEFAULT: empty subsystem, empty category. Every other logging site in the app uses a Logger with `subsystem: "com.adnan.augmentmereality"` and a category — metrics (GeoARSessionManager.swift:264-265), matte (SemanticOcclusionPass.swift:486), middepth (MidFieldDepthEstimator.swift:94), geospatial, assets, store, library, reactions, account. Consequence: the natural and universally-used capture predicate `subsystem == "com.adnan.augmentmereality"` silently drops the sentinel line. The round-2 verdict specifically ordered this instrument fixed BEFORE the field runs "so the instrument doesn't blame thermal throttling" — and it will be missing from the very log the owner collects, so a queue-wait stall will get attributed to thermal throttling anyway.
ownFindings.harm: Not a user-facing defect and not a ship blocker. It is a closure blocker: FT-28 and FT-31 exist to produce numbers, and one of the numbers the round-2 verdict named as decisive will not be in the capture unless the predicate is written differently than every other categorised line in this app. The failure is silent — an empty grep reads as "no capture-pool pressure," which is the same output as "the filter dropped it."
ownFindings.fix: One line, before the field runs, not after: `private static let log = Logger(subsystem: "com.adnan.augmentmereality", category: "sentinel")` on PersonSentinel and `Self.log.error("...")` at :64. Until then the field protocol must OR in a process predicate — my checklist does. While in the file, note the pre-existing (not round-3) tail that the `guard let self else { return }` at :50 skips the defer, so a deallocated sentinel never clears `busy`; harmless at app scope, worth a line in Wave E.

ownFindings.title: Even after the call-order fix, resume and the first tick still disagree inside the 1-second [pause, grace-end] window — the bare statement swap is not sufficient
ownFindings.trace: Reviewer-3 prescribes swapping markCameraVisible above startIfNeeded and explicitly warns against widening the resume term; reviewer-4 prescribes the swap plus one shared predicate. They conflict, and the residual decides it. After the swap, cameraDidAppear and appDidBecomeActive are correct (cameraVisible true at plan time). beginRevealWarmup (ARSessionHolder.swift:55-59, from ReceiveScreen.swift:50 and OnboardingView.swift:154) is not, and never marks visible. The pause fires at hide-edge + AppConfig.pauseGraceSeconds = 5.0 (ARSessionHolder.swift:113-115, AppConfig.swift:150) while the round-3 grace releases at hide-edge + 6.0 (GeoARSessionManager.swift:484-488). In the 1-second window between them the session is suspended AND cameraRecentlyVisible is still true, so a deep-link or onboarding reveal landing there computes resumePlan.reconstruction = false from `cameraVisible` (:545) while the first tick computes reconstruction = true from `cameraVisible || cameraRecentlyVisible` (:1215-1216 → :1338-1341) — two session.runs and a mesh rebuild again, on the reveal path, which is the one path where TTFO is measured.
ownFindings.harm: Narrow: a 1-second window requiring a link-open or onboarding reveal to land in it. But the harm class is identical to the HIGH (double reconfiguration + mesh teardown at the reveal instant), and the round-3 grace widening from 5.0 to 6.0 is what opened it — the two windows used to coincide. More importantly it proves the shape: two hand-written copies of one decision, keyed on two different visibility terms, is the defect. Patching the call order fixes two of three callers and leaves the third to be rediscovered in Wave E.
ownFindings.fix: Do not choose between the two reviewer prescriptions — the swap is necessary and the shared predicate is sufficient. Extract `nonisolated static func reconstructionDesired(supportsMesh:cameraVisibleOrRecent:pedestrian:thermalCritical:) -> Bool` and call it from both :543-550 and perceptionPlan:1338-1341; pass the visibility argument as the caller's intent (`cameraVisible || Self.cameraRecentlyVisible(now:lastVisible:)` at both sites, or the holder's own flag threaded through `resumeSession(cameraIntended:)`). Assert equality across the full 2^4 fact table, which is four lines of test and makes the two sides structurally incapable of disagreeing.

ownFindings.title: RENDER-LENS-1's dwell floor is unobservable — nothing logs the Metal pass attaching or detaching, so the field runs cannot measure the item round 3 built
ownFindings.trace: GeoARSessionManager.swift:1284-1299 attaches and detaches the pass via semanticPass?.setCallbacksActive(true/false), and SemanticOcclusionPass.setCallbacksActive:184-207 performs the RealityKit slot assignment. Grep for metricsLog lines mentioning pass/attach/detach/callback in GeoARSessionManager.swift returns nothing. Every other governor decision in this file emits: "Power tier → …" (:1186), "Perception recon=… person=… depth=…" (:865), "Window mode …" (:1141), "Capture format …" (:773), "Battery …· tier …· thermal …" (:1466). The one decision this round re-derived is the one with no line.
ownFindings.harm: The round-3 change to passShouldDetach moves the attach/detach cycle floor from an effective 15 s to 10 s — a ~1.5× rise in toggle rate on the exact surface RENDER-1 named as the race, deliberately traded for ADR-035's measured 5 s idle window. That trade is defensible, but its cost is on the unverifiable side of RSCH-1, and with no log line the owner cannot count the toggles during FT-28/FT-31 to see whether the rate is what the model predicts. The wave would close with the dwell floor asserted and never measured.

Tap-does-nothing, then moves-by-itself, then reverts on relaunch. That is the placement-correctness killer this product is built around, reachable by one tap on the primary panel, introduced by this commit.

One HIGH, also unanimous: the new `&& cameraVisible` conjunct at :545 is false on 100% of reachable resumes (markCameraVisible runs after startIfNeeded at both ARSessionHolder.swift:65 and :90; beginRevealWarmup never marks visible at all), so every warm resume runs a no-mesh configuration and then a second session.run one tick later — two reconfigurations and a mesh rebuild at the reveal instant, against the draw-over bar and on the killer-#1 measurement point. Round 2's ARPCFG-2 invariant is re-broken and its comment at :534-539 is now false.

The mitigating half is real and should be stated as plainly as the blockers. Five of the seven scoped items plus the ride-along are genuinely CLOSED at the mechanism level, verified independently: the hide-edge stamp with a 6.0 s grace that strictly outlasts the 5 s pause plus a 400 ms tick; the detach predicate with both conjuncts binding and stamped only on true attach edges; the ground-snap decline on the non-critical channel with slot discipline intact in both directions; both toast auto-clears guarding cancellation after the sleep; the sentinel's hold clock moved ahead of the enqueue with the latch replaced by a 60 s throttle read and written under one lock acquisition; and the mid-depth USE gate now literally sharing midFieldServiceable with the request side plus the sceneDepth capability term. The three new CallerClockTests are non-vacuous — each round-2 form fails at least one asserted row — and the caller-clock rule is honoured at the leaf. The build compiles clean for device and simulator.

So this is a two-line-family failure inside an otherwise clean closure diff, not a failed round. The fix set is roughly 40 lines across two files plus four tests. It does not warrant a fourth review round: it warrants a spot fix, the two pure extractions that make both defects table-testable (`editTarget(...)` and `reconstructionDesired(...)`), and then the field protocol below.
